\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Circuit Compression}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.LMN.CircuitCompression
\section{Overview}

This file develops Steps 6 and 7 of the LMN argument: once every layer-2 gate of a
depth-$d$ circuit can be switched to a width-$\ell$ CNF, two adjacent layers of the same
gate type can be merged, producing a depth-$(d-1)$ circuit of width at most $\ell$. The
module supplies the algebraic flattening identities (concatenation of CNF/DNF clause
lists preserves width and computes the conjunction/disjunction of the parts), the
resulting one-layer compression theorems, and the probabilistic one-step reduction
bounds obtained from the switching-lemma union bound under a Bernoulli random
restriction.

%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%%
\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Concatenation of a list of lists]
\lean{LMN.listConcat}
\label{LMN.listConcat}
\leanok
Flattens a list of lists $[\,\ell_1, \ell_2, \dots\,]$ into the single list
$\ell_1 \mathbin{+\!\!+} \ell_2 \mathbin{+\!\!+} \cdots$, defined by recursion on the
outer list. Used to merge the clause (or term) lists of several CNFs (or DNFs).
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Maximum term width bounded iff every term bounded]
\lean{LMN.width_le_iff_forall}
\label{LMN.width_le_iff_forall}
\leanok
\uses{Term, Term.width}
\difficulty{4}
Let $t_1, \dots, t_k$ be a finite list of terms, each a conjunction of literals, and let
$\ell$ be a natural number; write $w(t)$ for the width of a term (its number of
literals). Then the maximum width over the list, taken to be $0$ when the list is empty,
satisfies $\max_{1 \le i \le k} w(t_i) \le \ell$ if and only if $w(t) \le \ell$ for
every term $t$ in the list.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenating CNFs bounds their width]
\lean{LMN.cnf_concat_width_le}
\label{LMN.cnf_concat_width_le}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.width, LMN.listConcat}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\psi_1, \dots, \psi_s$ be CNF formulas over $n$ variables, and let $\ell$ be a
natural number such that each $\psi_i$ has width at most $\ell$. Then the CNF formula
obtained by concatenating all of their clause lists into a single list has width at most
$\ell$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Evaluation of concatenated CNF formulas]
\lean{LMN.cnf_concat_eval}
\label{LMN.cnf_concat_eval}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, LMN.listConcat}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\psi_1, \dots, \psi_k$ be CNF formulas over the variables $\{1, \dots, n\}$, and
form the single CNF formula obtained by concatenating all of their clause lists into
one. Then for every assignment $x \colon \{1,\dots,n\} \to
\{\text{true},\text{false}\}$, this concatenated formula evaluates to true at $x$ if and
only if every $\psi_i$ evaluates to true at $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Width bound for a concatenation of DNF formulas]
\lean{LMN.dnf_concat_width_le}
\label{LMN.dnf_concat_width_le}
\leanok
\uses{CNF, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.width, LMN.cnf_concat_width_le, LMN.listConcat, Term.width, cnfToDualDNF_width}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_s$ be DNF formulas over $n$ variables, and let $\ell$ be
a natural number such that each $\varphi_i$ has width at most $\ell$ (that is, every
term of every $\varphi_i$ contains at most $\ell$ literals). Then the DNF formula
obtained by concatenating all of their term lists into a single list of terms also has
width at most $\ell$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Concatenating DNFs evaluates as their disjunction]
\lean{LMN.dnf_concat_eval}
\label{LMN.dnf_concat_eval}
\leanok
\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, LMN.listConcat}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k$ be DNF formulas over $n$ variables, and let $x \in
\{0,1\}^n$ be a Boolean assignment. Form the single DNF whose term-list is the
concatenation of the term-lists of $\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k$. Then this concatenated
formula evaluates to true at $x$ if and only if at least one of the formulas $\varphi_i$
evaluates to true at $x$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Closure of bounded-width CNFs under conjunction]
\lean{LMN.compression_and_of_cnfs}
\label{LMN.compression_and_of_cnfs}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, LMN.cnf_concat_eval, LMN.cnf_concat_width_le, LMN.listConcat}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n$ and a width bound $\ell$, and let $f_1, \dots, f_k$ be Boolean functions on $n$
variables, each mapping an assignment $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ to a truth value. Suppose that
every $f_i$ is computed by some CNF formula of width at most $\ell$, that is, a
conjunction of clauses in which each clause has at most $\ell$ literals. Then their
conjunction $x \mapsto \bigwedge_{i=1}^{k} f_i(x)$ is also computed by a single CNF
formula of width at most $\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Closure of bounded-width DNFs under disjunction]
\lean{LMN.compression_or_of_dnfs}
\label{LMN.compression_or_of_dnfs}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.dnf_concat_eval, LMN.dnf_concat_width_le, LMN.listConcat}
\difficulty{3}
Let $f_1, \dots, f_m$ be Boolean functions on $\{0,1\}^n$, and let $\ell$ be a natural
number. Suppose that each $f_i$ is computed by some DNF formula of width at most $\ell$,
that is, a disjunction of terms in which every term has at most $\ell$ literals. Then
their disjunction $x \mapsto f_1(x) \lor \cdots \lor f_m(x)$ is also computed by a
single DNF formula of width at most $\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Failure probability for one-step CNF representation of DNF gates]
\lean{LMN.one_step_reduction_failure_bound}
\proofsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p003-b004
}
\label{LMN.one_step_reduction_failure_bound}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p008-b005
}
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.layer2_cnf_replaceability_union_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{2}
Fix an integer $w \ge 1$ and let $D_1, \dots, D_{s_2}$ be DNF formulas over $n \ge 1$
Boolean variables, each of width at most $w$, and suppose that within every term of
every $D_i$ no variable occurs more than once (distinct literals of a term have distinct
underlying variables, and no literal is repeated). Let $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ (so in
particular $p \le 1$), and draw a Bernoulli$(p)$ random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$
variables, in which each variable is independently left free with probability $p$ and
otherwise fixed to $0$ or to $1$, each with probability $\tfrac{1-p}{2}$. Then for any
target width $l$, the probability that some restricted gate $x \mapsto
D_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ fails to be computed by any CNF formula of width at most
$l$ is at most
\[
  s_2\!\left( \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{l} + \exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right) \right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {LMN.switching_bernoulli_union_bound}
  {direct}
  {switching-lemma}
  {pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002}
\uses{DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.switching_bernoulli_union_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_sum_one, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn, dtDepth}
\difficulty{5}
Fix an integer $n \ge 1$, let $w \ge 1$, and let $g_1, \dots, g_{s_2}$ be $s_2$ DNF
formulas on $n$ Boolean variables, each of width at most $w$. Assume that in every term
of every $g_i$ no literal is repeated and no two distinct literals share a variable. Let
$p \in \bbr$ satisfy $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ (so in particular $p \le 1$). Then,
under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction $\rho$ on the $n$ variables, the probability
that every restricted formula $x \mapsto g_i(\rho.\mathrm{extend}\,x)$ has decision-tree
depth at most $\ell$ is at least
\[
  1 - s_2\left( \left(\tfrac{1}{2}\right)^{\ell} + \exp\!\left(-np/3\right) \right).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Complementary events partition Bernoulli restriction probability]
\lean{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_complement}
\label{LMN.bernoulliRestrProb_complement}
\leanok
\uses{SwitchingLemma2.Restriction, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrWeight_sum_one}
\difficulty{4}
Fix $n$ and a parameter $p$ with $0 \le p \le 1$, and let $A$ be a predicate on
restrictions of $n$ variables. Writing $\Pr[A]$ for the probability that $A$ holds under
a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction, one has
\[
  \Pr[A] + \Pr[\neg A] = 1,
\]
where $\neg A$ is the predicate that holds exactly for those restrictions on which $A$
fails.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[One-step compression of DNF gates under random restriction]
\lean{LMN.one_step_reduction_with_compression}
\proofsource{switching-lemma}{
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p004-b002,
  pdf-b5e074215b9e-p003-b004
}
\label{LMN.one_step_reduction_with_compression}
\leanok
\proofsource{boolean-ch04-dnf-switching-lmn}{
  pdf-fc447f326910-p012-b004,
  pdf-fc447f326910-p013-b002
}
\uses{CNF, CNF.eval, CNF.width, DNF, DNF.eval, DNF.width, LMN.one_step_reduction_failure_bound, SwitchingLemma2.bernoulliRestrProb, SwitchingLemma2.restrictFn}
\difficulty{2}
Let $g_1,\dots,g_{s_2}$ be DNF formulas on $n \ge 1$ variables, each of width at most
$w$, where $w \ge 1$; assume that in every term of every $g_i$ any two literals on the
same variable coincide (so no term repeats a variable or contains both a literal and its
negation) and no literal occurs twice in the term. Fix a natural number $\ell$ and a
real $p$ with $0 < p \le \tfrac{1}{40w}$ and $p \le 1$. Then, for a Bernoulli-$p$ random
restriction $\rho$ of the $n$ variables,
\[
\Pr_\rho\Bigl[\text{for every } i,\ g_i|_\rho \text{ is computed by some CNF formula of
width } \le \ell\Bigr]
\;\ge\; 1 - s_2\left(\left(\tfrac12\right)^{\ell} +
\exp\!\left(-\tfrac{np}{3}\right)\right),
\]
where $g_i|_\rho$ is the restriction of $g_i$ by $\rho$ and a CNF formula $\psi$
*computes* $g_i|_\rho$ when $\psi$ and $g_i|_\rho$ agree on every input.
\end{theorem}
